## TL;DR

This pass built and launched the macOS RepoOS Hub, exercised the no-server first-run screen, discovered a running local RepoOS server, added it to an isolated registry, and confirmed the connected web view displays the sign-in page. The UI paths exercised did not show a crash or blank screen. The QA work also uncovered that XCTest launches the Hub as a test host and could write into the user's real application-support registry. That behavior is now isolated to a temporary per-process location during XCTest, and cleanup is checked by tests. The signed-in projects and tasks views remain unverified: the email-code flow could not be completed through the available automation, and human task #1174 has no result yet.

## Work and rationale

I used an Xcode build with signing disabled and a dedicated DerivedData location, as required for a local QA run without changing signing configuration. The app was launched through LaunchServices with `open -n` and an explicit `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` pointing to scratch storage. That kept app-driven registry writes out of the user's normal Hub data. Window inspection and screenshots were limited to the Hub window using its window ID; no full-screen capture was made. The captures were kept outside the repository because the repository's secret scan rejects oversized compressed binary payloads, while the observed screens and outcomes are described in the QA record.

The first-run screen rendered with no registered servers. The add-server sheet found the running `repoos` server on localhost through the saved-server discovery path and health probe. Adding it persisted a healthy entry in the isolated registry and showed it in the sidebar. The connected server's embedded web view displayed the RepoOS sign-in page. This establishes that launch, initial rendering, discovery, health checking, persistence, and the unauthenticated connection view work on this build.

During the XCTest run, I found the test host was using the normal application-support directory when no override was present. That caused a write to the real Hub registry. The available before-state was incomplete, so I recorded the observed registry changes and did not guess at or overwrite values that had not been captured. The fix makes the test host use a unique temporary support directory unless an explicit override is supplied. An explicit override remains highest priority so tests can choose a controlled location. The resolution cases are covered in a table-driven test, and focused coverage verifies the temporary directory is removed. Cleanup errors are propagated and logged rather than silently ignored. The later suite run passed with the additional test, and the real registry modification time remained unchanged during that isolated follow-up.

I also recorded the direct-executable launch experiment. A process started, but the early window check found only menu-bar-sized windows rather than the content window. LaunchServices did produce a normal content window, so the direct-exec observation is documented as unexplained and not treated as a demonstrated application crash. It remains a follow-up for anyone who depends on launching the binary outside LaunchServices.

## Approaches tried

- Built the `RepoOSHub` scheme in Debug with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` and a task-specific DerivedData path.
- Launched the built app via `open -n --env REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY=…`, then inspected the Hub window and drove its first-run and add-server flows.
- Tested direct execution of the app binary as a separate launch path. It did not produce a content window during the short observation period; the normal LaunchServices path was used for the rest of the QA run.
- Ran the XCTest suite before and after isolating test-host storage. The initial run exposed the real-registry write; the follow-up verified the isolated behavior and directory cleanup.
- Attempted the email-code sign-in flow using synthetic input and native sheet automation. The sign-in field did not accept the automated entry, so this did not reach authenticated projects or tasks screens. I left that criterion explicitly open and created/linked human task #1174 instead of inferring success from another QA pass or inventing a result.

## Challenges and blockers

The material blocker is authenticated UI verification. The current run reached the sign-in page but did not complete the email-code interaction. Review pass 5 confirms #1174 has no results and requires the signed-in projects and tasks observations before sign-off. The live board currently shows #1174 as a human-assigned inbox task. A human needs to start and complete that task against this build, record the build identity and both screen results, and report any visible errors. Until then, the acceptance criterion is not complete.

The direct-exec launch behavior is also unexplained. It is outside the LaunchServices launch path used by the app run and has not been tied to a crash, but it should be revisited if direct execution is a supported way to start the Hub. The accidental initial XCTest registry write could not be fully reversed because its prior selected-server value was not recorded; the QA record preserves that limitation rather than claiming restoration.

## Key learnings

XCTest's app-host process needs an explicit storage boundary: tests that launch the application should not silently inherit the user's normal application-support path. The override-first, XCTest-temporary, normal-launch resolution order makes this distinction predictable and testable. Directory cleanup should fail visibly, since a silent cleanup failure can leave test data accumulating without a clear cause.

For native app QA, proving that the sign-in page renders is useful but does not prove authenticated screens work. The projects and tasks views require a real email-code sign-in, so their verification must remain assigned to a human with access to the account and device UI. Similarly, a separate launch mode should be reported as an observation until its behavior is reproduced and understood.

The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on source tree `409d6fd0a9b5898f0fcad395fd87226067c3ba33`. Remote build, changed-path tests (96 tests across four test files, plus the always-run timing file), format, lint, UI smoke, and the local safety guards passed. The local summary correctly marked the test step as already run remotely. The report is bound to that checked source tree; it does not claim the human sign-in criterion is complete.
